title: TV card rebuild: three ways to show the remote

steps.headline: With the remote closed, which TV card do you like best?
steps.notice: Both themes (Golden Sunbreak and Crème) are shown. Netflix is playing, so the app buttons show Prime Video where Netflix would be. The remote is now a small icon beside the power button.
steps.risk: Closed, all three look almost the same except the app buttons: option C hides them until the remote opens.

variants.label: Machined dial
variants.summary: A dial that looks like brushed metal, with engraved arrows and a domed OK button.
variants.risk: Heaviest and most solid-looking; the metal can feel out of place beside the soft glass cards.

variants.label: Glass jog wheel
variants.summary: A frosted glass wheel in four quarters.
variants.risk: The lit quarter hides behind your thumb on a phone; the sweep is a little showy the first few times.

variants.label: Floating ring
variants.summary: Just a thin outline ring with small arrows, no filled disc.
variants.risk: Lightest and calmest, but with no fill the arrows are less obviously buttons; closed, the card has no app buttons at all.

steps.path: Home > Media > the TV card > remote icon
steps.headline: With the remote open, which dial looks the most premium?
steps.notice: The dial sits above the volume bar, inside the Now playing panel. Back and Home flank the skip and play buttons.
steps.risk: The panel is taller when open, so cards below it move down.

variants.label: Machined dial
variants.summary: A dial that looks like brushed metal, with engraved arrows and a domed OK button.
variants.risk: Heaviest and most solid-looking; the metal can feel out of place beside the soft glass cards.

variants.label: Glass jog wheel
variants.summary: A frosted glass wheel in four quarters.
variants.risk: The lit quarter hides behind your thumb on a phone; the sweep is a little showy the first few times.

variants.label: Floating ring
variants.summary: Just a thin outline ring with small arrows, no filled disc.
variants.risk: Lightest and calmest, but with no fill the arrows are less obviously buttons; closed, the card has no app buttons at all.

steps.headline: Press the remote icon, then an app button. Which reveal and app swap feels best?
steps.notice: Open and close the remote a few times, press the arrows and OK, then press HBO Max or Disney+: the app on the TV leaves the row and Prime Video slides into its place.
steps.risk: All three add short movement (about a third of a second) and all stop if the computer is set to reduce motion. The pretend TV answers app presses after a short delay, like a real one.

variants.label: Machined dial
variants.summary: The dial grows out of the remote icon with a small spring. The app that leaves shrinks away and Prime drops in from above.
variants.risk: The dial travels the furthest, so it is the most movement on screen.

variants.label: Glass jog wheel
variants.summary: The panel stretches down while the volume row slides lower and the wheel fades in with a sweep of light. The old app slides out left, Prime slides in from the right.
variants.risk: The panel's stretch moves everything beneath it for a moment.

variants.label: Floating ring
variants.summary: The ring unfolds down from the header like a flap, then the app buttons fade up. The old app lifts away and Prime rises into place. Presses ripple.
variants.risk: The flap is a 3-D turn, which some people find flashy on a small card.
